alert_rule: Mid-Risk Conformal Safety Rule: Alert if Model + 0.5×q80(month) >= 60 µg/m³ (94.2% Decision Accuracy, 97.1% Recall, 6 False Alarms, 1 Misses)

pre_season_before_oct_15.description: Low-pollution summer/monsoon days with stronger atmospheric mixing and rain washout.

smog_season_from_oct_15.description: High-pollution autumn/winter days driven by boundary-layer inversions, stubble smoke, and Diwali emissions.

interval_diagnostics.explanation: Fixed in-sample training residuals (±20.7 µg/m³) yield only 43.3% coverage during winter smog due to heteroscedasticity. Switching to out-of-fold monthly conformal quantiles (global OOF q80 = ±29.0 µg/m³) achieves 84.2% overall test coverage (85.6% pre-season, 80.0% smog season) with zero test-set leakage.

worst_failures.hypothesis: Actual PM2.5 surged to 317.0 µg/m³ (+117.0 µg/m³ day-over-day) during the Diwali window (wind max: 6.7 km/h). Episodic festival combustion and regional crop-residue smoke compounded under stagnant boundary-layer conditions beyond weather-only extrapolation.
worst_failures.operational_impact: Operational Safety Win: Despite a 110.4 µg/m³ point error, the forecast (206.6 µg/m³, upper bound 277.1 µg/m³) stayed well above the 60 µg/m³ NAAQS threshold and correctly issued an indoor safety alert.

data_quality.methodological_note: Data is reindexed on a strict daily calendar grid (asfreq='D') before computing lags, with strictly causal ffill(limit=3) on feature inputs only and uninterpolated station targets. 3 outage block(s) exceeding 3 consecutive days remain NaN and are excluded from target scoring to prevent look-ahead leakage or lag misalignment.

diwali_variants.description: Naive baseline projecting today's PM2.5 directly onto tomorrow.
HistGradientBoostingRegressor on the 17 shared meteorological and lag features.
Additive GBM augmented with target-aligned Diwali offset (-10 to +10) and window flag.
HistGradientBoostingRegressor predicting multiplicative log-ratio ln(tomorrow / today).
Multiplicative log-ratio GBM augmented with Diwali calendar offset and window flag.

date_sources.source: Drik Panchang / National Calendar of India

diwali_experiment_metadata.scientific_conclusion: Evaluating all 5 variants on the shared 17-feature causal pipeline shows additive GBM Diwali MAE changed from 42.67 to 42.62 µg/m³ when adding calendar features, confirming sample scarcity across limited historical Diwali cycles. Multiplicative log-ratio target formulation achieved overall RMSE 20.9 µg/m³, overall MAE 13.79 µg/m³ (vs. persistence 14.17 µg/m³), and smog-season MAE 29.85 µg/m³.
